judged_text: Both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (z.string().toString() on a ZodString instance), so the schema declares only access_token plus an optional '[object Object]' property, and zod's default unknown-key stripping discards the expiry date and every other field the design says the sync endpoint returns. With sharing enabled, Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-263) and Zoom persist parsed data containing only access_token and the dummy refresh_token; expiry_date is never refreshed, stays in the past, and refreshAccessToken — a sync-endpoint HTTP call plus a credential DB write — runs on every single calendar operation.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, minimumTokenResponseSchema defines two computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately and become a single literal property name (very likely "[object Object]"), not an index signature. As a result the schema effectively only requires `access_token` and does not preserve fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, any real expiry field returned by the sync endpoint will be dropped from `refreshTokenResponse.data`. The calling code (e.g., office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials; zoom similarly uses it) would therefore persist credentials without a refreshed expiry, causing repeated refresh attempts and extra DB writes when the stored expiry remains stale.
